Lowest NFL legs: 2026 season

No, they don't all hit, in any week. Across 9 weeks of the regular season (136 finished games through Nov 8), the lowest offered line hit 3667 of 4934 times (74.3%) on player yardage and volume stats. Passing yards was the best stat at 92.4%, but it missed 20 times. No game had every leg hit. Players who left injured are excluded.

Every lowest leg

How to read this

  • Every finished regular-season game is included. Games with a parlay above aren't, since they haven't been played.
  • Results are the exchange's settlements. Actual stats are from ESPN and matched 9950 of 9959 legs where the player was in the box score. 6 of the 9 differences are fantasy-point calculations. The settlement is what's counted.
  • Price is the midpoint of the last price snapshot before kickoff. Returns use the pregame ask price, before fees. Thin books may not have filled at those prices.
  • 342 legs from players who never took a snap are marked VOID and left out of hit rates.
  • Injury data is weaker for older games. Most games use only ESPN's play-by-play notes (injured with no return and no later touches). ESPN's injury report is a current snapshot, so it's only used for the Nov 8 games, which is why Week 9 has more removals. A player who left without a note can still be counted in older games.
  • "Possible silent exit" means a leg priced 80¢ or more but the player had no touches after halftime and no injury note. Some were just game script or benchings. Those players stay in by default, and the table shows the effect of removing them.
  • Depth roles are inferred, not official. ESPN only publishes today's depth chart, so each player is ranked within their team and position by that game's pregame ladder (rushing yards for RBs, receiving yards for WRs and TEs). As a check, the top-ranked player led their group in usage that game 86% of the time for RBs (carries), 70% for WRs and 85% for TEs (targets). Players who didn't play are not ranked, so the next player moves up.
  • A benched quarterback is not treated as injured. Those legs still count.
